title: A former preacher becomes Joseph Smith’s scribe and partner
setting: Sidney Rigdon led a reformed Baptist congregation in northeastern Ohio. In November 1830 missionaries preached there, and Rigdon and many members joined the Church. In early December Rigdon and Edward Partridge traveled to New York to meet Joseph Smith. Joseph dictated this revelation on 7 December 1830 at or near Fayette. He had been revising the Bible since June 1830, and his earlier scribes had other duties.
summary: The voice speaks as Jesus Christ, crucified so believers may become one with him as he is with the Father. It tells Sidney Rigdon that God has seen his works and prepared him for a greater work. It compares him to John, sent to prepare the way without knowing it. He had baptized without the Holy Ghost following; now those he baptizes will receive it by laying on of hands. The revelation promises miracles to believers and says the weak and unlearned will thresh the nations. It says the gospel came through Joseph, blessed in weakness, who holds keys while he abides in Christ. Sidney is to watch over Joseph, write for him, and not forsake him. If Sidney does not write, Joseph will prophesy and Sidney will preach and prove his words from the prophets.

contextNote.title: A scribe for the Bible revision
contextNote.text: Joseph’s scribes for his Bible revision, Oliver Cowdery and John Whitmer, had been given other duties. Verse 20 fills that gap: Sidney is commanded to “write for him”. The same verse says the scriptures will be given “even as they are in mine own bosom”. Verse 19 makes the job more than copying, since Sidney must watch over Joseph “that his faith fail not”. Verse 22 adds a personal bond: “tarry with him” and “forsake him not”. In this passage, writing for Joseph means being his steady partner in receiving scripture.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 30–36 uses verses 13–15 and 24 to teach that members are called to witness of Jesus Christ. Verse 13 says the Lord calls “the weak things of the world”; how do verses 17–18 show the same pattern in Joseph’s calling?
reviewNote: Read all 27 verses. Official heading gives 7 December 1830, at or near Fayette, to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon, with Rigdon replacing Cowdery and Whitmer as Bible scribe. JSP introduction confirmed Rigdon and Partridge’s early-December arrival from Ohio. Kirtland is included as the region of Rigdon’s Ohio congregation (he lived at Mentor nearby). “John” in v. 4 is taken as John the Baptist. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
